acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Goblins family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Goblin King, T5, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Warren Lootworks Monarch (Sovereign) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Sits upright on a welded throne of recognizable stolen loot above a coin dais, wearing a crown made from fused crowns, a cloak stitched from captured flags, and rings on every finger; the throne's crude winch, chute, and door press extend the treasure silhouette into a working war machine.

Signature mechanic: Royal Lootworks: the welded throne-dais has three exposed stations fueled by scrap that Cutters deliver. At each command beat the King points to one station: the cage winch brings fresh Runts from a warren hatch, the armory chute outfits a surviving Runt as a Cutter, or the door press repairs a Raider's broken Claimed Door. Between cycles, a captured-flag decree orders Runts to rush, Cutters to collect, Raiders to barricade, and any Warboss to defend the active station. Destroyed stations stay disabled and loss of all three forces the King off the throne.
battlefieldDuty: Operate a command-and-production boss encounter that converts carried battlefield scrap into reinforcements, promotions, and repaired formation tools while issuing role-specific orders from the royal dais.
constructionDimensions: Materials and load paths combine scavenged gear with stolen masonry: cracked paving-stone plates, door lintels, ore sacks, pit props, and rope cages are lashed onto rusted equipment with visibly strained joints.

Silhouette and locomotion become low and load-bearing: wide rubble-packed shields, dragging stone counterweights, planted braces, falling grit, and short dust compressions show when a Goblin is anchored or mobile.
counterplay: Intercept scrap-carrying Cutters, cut the bright drive rope before the bell finishes, destroy the exposed selected station, or lure its defenders away; each broken station removes one production option, and an empty dais makes the dismounted King fight without replacement troops or repaired doors. Affinity signal: Taut support ropes and pale fracture seams appear at the loaded edge before an anchored action; severing a rope or striking the seam collapses the brace and opens the Goblin's back.
forbiddenTreatments: Brown recolor without masonry, load, or locomotion changes
Glow-only earth treatment without masonry, load-bearing structure, or fracture behavior
Seamless noble stone armor that conceals scavenged bindings
Permanent rock anatomy that erases the wiry Goblin silhouette
identityInvariants: Short, hunched, long-armed humanoid silhouette with an oversized head and pointed ears, disproportionately large hands and feet, hooked nose, and crowded crooked teeth.
Sickly green or grey-green skin against muddy browns, rust-orange, dull iron, and sparse accents of stolen gold.
Every carried object reads as stolen, scavenged, or crudely repaired: rags, patched leather, cracked wood, rusted scrap metal, bone, and rope rather than purpose-built matching equipment.
Loot is the status language: mismatched helmets, coin necklaces, teeth, rings, captured banners, and trophies accumulate with rank.
Posture and finish communicate hierarchy, from a knock-kneed cringing crouch to an upright swagger amid increasingly prestigious plunder.
telegraph: The King rises beneath the crown of fused crowns, points a ring-heavy hand, and yanks one captured flag; the selected station's stolen bell rings while its gears visibly spool and the matching lower forms shout and turn toward their ordered route.
